text:
maria: Heads-up from the perf squad: we shipped the "quant-ladder" + dynamic-length packer prototype into canary this morning. TL;DR: p50 -2%, p95 -12%, p99 -15%, token-cost ~-14% on mixed web/chat traffic for gpt-medium-v2. :sparkles:

maria: What we did: implemented a per-request quantization ladder that picks a safe quant level (fp16 -> int8 -> int4) per-layer based on a fast uncertainty estimator, combined with a length-aware packer that groups similar decode-length requests to reduce padding and microbatch fragmentation. The ladder falls back to fp16 when estimated KL divergence > 0.02.

ashwin: Nice. How stable are the quality metrics? Any measurable drift on our eval set?

maria: We ran the standard 15k prompt eval + blind A/B with human raters on 300 pairs. Automated metrics show a median BLEU-like proxy change <0.4% and avg response perplexity delta within the 0.02 KL ceiling. Human raters flagged 3 examples of subtle phrasing shifts (we flagged those for product).

rachel: Bench numbers please (canary vs baseline).

maria: From the bench harness (1% traffic sample + synthetic mix):
```
baseline (runtime/main): p50 45ms, p95 160ms, p99 420ms, token-cost=1.00
canary  (quant-ladder/v1): p50 44ms, p95 141ms, p99 357ms, token-cost=0.86
diff: p95 -19ms (-11.9%), p99 -63ms (-15%), cost -14%
```

ashwin: Great tail cut. Do we know if p99 gains come more from shorter decode (int4) or better packing?

maria: It's both. For long-context chat flows the ladder drops into int8/int4 and saves decode kernel time; for short queries the improved length-bucketing increases coalescence so batch efficiency goes up. We instrumented per-step time and saw roughly 8% kernel speedup attributable to quant kernels and 6% throughput lift from packing.

rachel: Any runtime surprises? memory pressure, scheduling, or vendor kernel glitches?

maria: A few notes: some older GPU driver versions had non-deterministic int4 kernel times -> we gate the int4 path on driver >= 530.12. Also saw a transient where the packer created very small batches for a handful of microservices; we deployed a small hysteresis to avoid churn. No OOMs.

deploy-bot: deploy: quant-ladder/v1 -> canary on pool-gpu-b (3 instances) at 2025-01-18T09:12:03Z

rachel: Rollout plan? feature flags?

maria: Rollout: 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% across 72h with automated checks. Feature flags: "runtime.quant_ladder.enabled" (canary default=true), "runtime.quant_ladder.max_kl" (default=0.02), "runtime.quant_ladder.min_decodes" (default=8). We also added "runtime.quant_ladder.driver_min_version" to prevent int4 on unsupported infra. Automatic rollback if p99 or token-cost regress beyond thresholds.

ashwin: Is this safe for Dedicated customers?

maria: For Dedicated we added an opt-in toggle in the admin panel. Product will handle outreach; default is off for Dedicated until we complete per-customer determinism tests.

rachel: Can you paste the exact rollout commands for ops?

maria: Sure:
```
# canary
redwood deploy set-tag --pool pool-gpu-b --tag quant-ladder/v1 --pct 2
sleep 3600
redwood deploy set-tag --pool pool-gpu-b --tag quant-ladder/v1 --pct 10
# increase to 30% after 12h if stable, and to 100% after 72h
```

maria: Artifacts: eval CSVs and kernel traces uploaded to s3://ci-redwood/benchmarks/quant-ladder/v1 and a short runbook in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood/quant-ladder). I've also added a dashboard tile in Console for "avg decoded tokens" and "quant-level distribution" per model.

rachel: Please add a short blurb to #eng-notices and cc finance for the cost-saving writeup. We'll need billing estimates for reserved capacity customers.

maria: Will do. Planning to run a focused 24h cost sim against dedicated traces next week.

ashwin: :rocket: huge work. Quick follow-up: add a perf counter for "int4 fallbacks" so we can audit cases where KL threshold forced a higher precision.

maria: Good idea — adding that to the telemetry spec now.

rachel: Congrats team. Small ask: drop the human rater notes into the benchmark folder so product can triage.

maria: Done. Closing timeline: start 2% canary now, target full roll in 72h with rollback gates. I'll post updates in this thread as we progress."
